page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highcpu-4 is an x86_64 compute-oriented virtual machine provisioned with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of system memory. Operating at a ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per dedicated vCPU, this configuration emphasizes CPU density over expansive memory capacity. The instance includes no onboard local storage and requires remote network storage for operational filesystems. It operates without dedicated hardware accelerators or GPUs.

Because memory is capped at 8.0 GB, memory footprint management is a critical factor when designing workloads for this machine type. System architects should anticipate remote disk latency and bandwidth constraints since all persistence relies on external storage volumes. The 1:2 core-to-memory ratio provides a resource-dense setup that minimizes unutilized memory overhead for compute-focused tasks.

This instance profile fits workloads that require dedicated processing capacity without excessive memory demand. Common target use cases include CI/CD build agents, batch computation, web serving tiers, and containerized microservices where execution tasks remain strictly bounded within 8.0 GB of memory.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highcpu-4 is a compute-centric virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs paired with 8.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 CPU-to-memory ratio with 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, necessitating persistent network-attached block volumes for system operation, and contains zero GPUs. Without integrated storage or accelerator hardware, the machine profile prioritizes efficient execution of CPU-bound processes without excess memory allocation overhead. This profile aligns directly with workloads such as build pipelines, lightweight web application hosting, distributed batch processing, and stateless microservices.
